full_text_en:
EOS Engineering Co. (USA) v. Shanxi Xinjiang Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang County People's Government, Shanxi Branch of Bank of China, et al. — dispute over tort

[Ruling Summary]

Where a party, after obtaining a final judgment from a people's court in a civil action it has initiated, subsequently files another civil action against the same defendants based on the same subject matter, the court shall rule to dismiss the action on the ground that it does not meet the conditions for acceptance.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
No. 2 (2003) Min Si Zhong Zi

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): EOS Engineering Co. (USA). Domicile: 302 Oak Road, Murrieta, California, USA.

Legal Representative: Neal Stevens, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the company.

In the dispute over tort filed by EOS Engineering Co. (USA) against Shanxi Xinjiang Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang County People's Government, and Shanxi Branch of Bank of China, the appellant appealed against the Civil Ruling (2002) Jin Li Min Chu Zi No. 1 rendered by the Shanxi High People's Court. This court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Wang Yun presiding as the presiding judge, and Acting Judges Chen Jizhong and Gao Xiaoli participating in the deliberation, to try this case.

The court of first instance found that: EOS Engineering Co. had previously filed an action in the same court in 1999 concerning the same legal facts under the claim of "refund of project funds", and subsequently applied to change the claim to "unjust enrichment". After a hearing, the court rendered the Civil Judgment (2001) Jin Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 on April 4, 2001, dismissing the claims of EOS Engineering Co. EOS Engineering Co., dissatisfied with that judgment, appealed to the Supreme People's Court. During the appeal, it filed a written application to withdraw the appeal, and the Supreme People's Court rendered the Civil Ruling (2001) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 64 in November 2001, granting the withdrawal of the appeal. Consequently, the Civil Judgment (2001) Jin Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 of the court of first instance became legally effective. According to the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, a party who disagrees with a legally effective judgment of a people's court should file a complaint or apply for retrial in accordance with the law. Accordingly, the court of first instance, pursuant to Article 112 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, ruled not to accept the action filed by EOS Engineering Co.

EOS Engineering Co., dissatisfied with the above ruling, appealed, arguing:

1. The ruling of the first instance violated legal procedures. EOS Engineering Co. filed the action for tort against Shanxi Xinjiang Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang County People's Government, and Shanxi Branch of Bank of China with the Shanxi High People's Court on February 4, 2002. On April 1, 2002, the Case Filing Division of that court, after examination, accepted the case in accordance with the law. EOS Engineering Co. paid the court costs as required. After the case was assigned to the Fourth Civil Division, the presiding judge served copies of the complaint on the defendants. Subsequently, the Fourth Civil Division returned the case to the Case Filing Division, which ruled not to accept the case. If the Fourth Civil Division, during the trial, believed that the plaintiff's claims were unfounded, it should have dismissed the plaintiff's claims, rather than returning the case to the Case Filing Division. This practice constituted a procedural violation.

2. The ruling of the first instance deprived EOS Engineering Co. of its civil procedural rights. According to Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, an action must meet four conditions to be accepted, and the action filed by EOS Engineering Co. in this case fully satisfied those conditions. EOS Engineering Co. had previously filed an action in the same court in 1999 concerning the same facts under the claim of "refund of project funds", and later changed the claim to "unjust enrichment". The court of first instance dismissed EOS Engineering Co.'s claims. EOS Engineering Co., dissatisfied, appealed to the Supreme People's Court. During the appeal, it realized that the case did not fall under "unjust enrichment" but rather under a tort legal relationship, and therefore filed an application to withdraw the appeal. It was against this background that EOS Engineering Co. filed the new action based on tort. The action based on tort is a different case from the concluded case of unjust enrichment. The ruling of the first instance, which refused to accept the case on the ground that "a party who disagrees with a legally effective judgment should file a complaint or apply for retrial", deprived EOS Engineering Co. of its procedural rights. Therefore, EOS Engineering Co. requested that the ruling of the first instance be set aside and that the Shanxi High People's Court resume the trial of this case.

This court holds that: In the present case, the plaintiff at first instance, EOS Engineering Co., based on the same facts and against the same defendants, successively filed an action for "unjust enrichment" and an action for "tort" damages with the court of first instance. Although the grounds for the actions differed, the substantive subject matter was the same, namely, EOS Engineering Co. sought to resolve the dispute arising from its remittance of USD 1 million to the Preparatory Office of the Shanxi Xinjiang County Power Plant in 1995 by filing a lawsuit in the people's court. With respect to this subject matter, EOS Engineering Co. first sought the return of USD 1 million and interest on the ground of "unjust enrichment". The court of first instance rendered the Civil Judgment (2001) Jin Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2. EOS Engineering Co., dissatisfied, appealed, and then withdrew the appeal, whereupon the Civil Judgment (2001) Jin Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 became legally effective. If EOS Engineering Co. still disagreed with that substantive judgment, it could only seek relief through filing a complaint or applying for retrial. Now, EOS Engineering Co., on the ground of "tort", has initiated another action with the same subject matter, violating the principle of "no double jeopardy" (res judicata). According to Article 111, paragraph (5) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, "Where a party brings another action in a case where a judgment or ruling has already become legally effective, the court shall instruct the plaintiff to file a complaint, unless the court has granted the withdrawal of the action." Therefore, the people's court should not accept the action filed by EOS Engineering Co. based on the same facts and against the same defendants on the ground of "tort". The court of first instance correctly determined this. However, according to Article 139 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, "Where an action does not meet the conditions for acceptance, the people's court shall rule not to accept it. If, after filing, it is discovered that the action does not meet the conditions for acceptance, the court shall rule to dismiss the action." In this case, since the court of first instance had already docketed the case, it should not have ruled not to accept it, but rather should have ruled to dismiss the action. The ruling of the first instance was erroneous on this point and should be corrected. The first ground of appeal raised by the appellant is well-founded and is supported by this court; the second ground of appeal is not well-founded and is not supported by this court.

In summary, pursuant to Article 154 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 139 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this court rules as follows:

1. The Civil Ruling (2002) Jin Li Min Chu Zi No. 1 of the Shanxi High People's Court is set aside;

2. The action filed by EOS Engineering Co. is dismissed.

The court costs for the second instance, RMB 50, shall be borne by the appellant, EOS Engineering Co.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yun
Acting Judge: Chen Jizhong
Acting Judge: Gao Xiaoli

Issued on August 12, 2003

Clerk: Yang Honglei

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

Wang Yun, Senior Judge: Born in 1955, Master of Laws. Served as Deputy Chief Judge of the Fourth Civil Division of the Supreme People's Court from 2003.
